title: How to Engage Politics Without Losing Your Soul
excerpt: You can care about justice without making a kingdom of this world your god. The ancient creed that got Christians killed was political, and it set them free.
body:
Watch your body when the other side wins an election. The drop in the stomach, the dread that feels almost spiritual. Watch when your side wins: the surge of vindication, the sense that the country has been saved. Those are not the responses of a citizen casting a vote. They are the responses of a worshiper whose god has been threatened or enthroned. Most of us, if we are honest, recognize the feeling. And the feeling is the warning.

Something has happened to the believer, and it happened so gradually we did not feel it occur. Politics stopped being one arena of life and became the arena, the lens that sorts who our friends are, which Christians are sound, and whether the future is hope or catastrophe. We did not decide to make a kingdom of this world ultimate. We absorbed it the way you absorb a fever. And now a political identity sits where a religious one used to be, often wearing its clothes.

## The tell: the tribe now reads the Bible

Here is the symptom that should alarm us. For many believers, the tribe now reads the Bible instead of the Bible reading the tribe. You can tell, before a Christian opens his mouth on any subject, what he will say, because you already know how he votes. The politics has become the fixed thing, and the faith bends to fit it. Without quite noticing, we let the parties disciple us. They got there first, more present and more emotionally insistent than the slow voice of Scripture.

Losing your soul in politics does not look like a dramatic apostasy. It looks like excusing in your own side what you condemn in the other. It looks like receiving comfortable lies because they serve your team. It looks like contempt you have learned to feel righteous about.

## Render to Caesar, and not one inch more

When they tried to trap Jesus on taxes, he asked whose image was on the coin. Caesar's, they said. Then render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's. The line is exact and devastating. Caesar gets his coin, his taxes, his real and limited authority. But the image on the coin is Caesar's, and the image on you is God's, and what bears God's image belongs to God alone. Caesar gets the coin. He does not get the worshiper.

This is the whole of political sanity. The state is real, ordained, owed honest engagement. The state is not ultimate, and the moment it asks for the allegiance that belongs to God, the Christian says no, the way the martyrs said no to the pinch of incense before Caesar's image. Polycarp died over that distinction. Engage politics, yes. But know where the coin ends and the worship begins.

## Hope makes you free

The gospel gives the believer a freedom no party can. Because your ultimate hope rests on a King already enthroned, you can engage with energy and without idolatry, with conviction and without despair. You can lose an election without losing your world, because your world was never up for a vote. You can love your opponent as a neighbor rather than hate him as an enemy, because your security does not depend on defeating him.

This is not apathy. Indifference is not the goal and detachment is not the gospel. It is the calm of a person who has read the end of the story and knows which kingdom stands. From that calm you can work hard for a just cause and still sleep, because the outcome rests in hands that were nailed for you and not in the hands of an electorate.

## Tell the truth to your own side

The deepest test of whether the faith owns the politics or the politics owns the faith is whether you can name the sins of your own tribe. The idolater excuses in his side what he condemns in the other, because the tribe is his god and a god can do no wrong. The believer set free can say the hard, costly word to the people whose approval he most wants, because he answers to a higher King than the crowd. It will get you called a traitor by your own. That is the price of having only one Lord.

## This week

Notice your body the next time the news breaks, and name the dread or the vindication honestly as worship rather than citizenship. Then do two things. Pray by name for a leader you did not vote for, that God would grant them wisdom. And say one true, costly thing about your own side's sins, out loud, to someone in it. Notice how hard the second one is. The difficulty is the measure of how much the tribe already owns.
